headline: The Texas utility regulator has sued the state attorney general's office to keep the locations of data centers and crypto mines secret.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: a real legal fight over data center transparency, but a narrow records dispute with no ruling yet.
importance_line: Texans and journalists trying to see how much water and electricity data centers use are affected, and the commission argues disclosure could aid attackers, but the suit covers only two data fields and no court has ruled.
summary: The Texas Tribune reports that the Public Utility Commission of Texas filed suit on 5 Oct 2026 against Attorney General Ken Paxton's office, asking a Travis County judge to block release of the county and water-planning area of data centers and crypto mines, which the commission says could aid terrorists when combined with other survey data. The attorney general's office had twice ruled that the commission failed to show the information is protected, and the Tribune says one of its reporters is among those who requested the records.
notes: Read in full. Filed Monday 5 Oct 2026, reported 6 Oct inside the scan window. The Tribune discloses that a Tribune reporter is among the records requesters.
